newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up, traded at $24.35/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas up, traded at $24.35/bbl.

text.p: Singapore's gasoline prices edged up higher on a spate of firm bids but some traders were mixed as the market appeared to be awashed with supplies, traders said on Monday.
Near market close, a cargo of 95 octane supplies was traded between two Japanese traders at $24.35 per barrel for May 24-28 loading.
The prices was deemed firm by some traders who thought that the market was bearish with unsold supplies still seeking market outlets.
At the sidelines, a bid for 92-octane supplies was heard at $23.75 and a 97-octane cargo was bid at $24.95 per barrel against no offers.
Some traders were cautious, waiting for results of Taiwan's tender to buy 250,000 barrel cargo for June 11-30 delivery before moving their cargoes. The tender closed May 5 and is valid for two days.
Thailand's Star refinery was also heard to be offering gasoline supplies but details were unclear.
Talks were thin in the naphtha market.
Naphtha swaps for May and June were quoted at $21.00/$21.20 and $21.20/$21.400 down from Friday's quotes.
Traders expected the market to pick up later this month after North Asian's ethylene plants resume operations after thier recent shutdowns.
